findings.note: DiffRuns collapses judge calls that share (node, iter, kind, input_hash) but differ by index/model. collect() keys rows on those four fields only (diff.go:72-97) and assigns row.A/row.B unconditionally, so the last matching call in a run overwrites the earlier one and that earlier call disappears from the report entirely. This is reachable through the swappable-judge path the branch adds: Machine.RecordLLMCall (machine.go:1061) stamps Index = NextIndex("judge@<iter>"), so running `fsm judge --run` twice on the same input in one iteration - e.g. the same kind against two models, which is the point of swappable judges - produces exactly such a pair. CallSide already carries Index (diff.go:38), showing a call is identified by index, yet index and model are excluded from the key. The comparison report is an auditability artifact, so silently dropping a call is worse than reporting it unmatched. No test covers duplicate input hashes: the sort assertion at fork_test.go:740 asserts strictly increasing InputHash within a node/iter/kind, which presumes uniqueness.

findings.note: The codex arm has no fatal classification. The HTTP arm returns immediately when classify() yields classFatal (judge.go:543), but codexJudge.Call retries every non-zero exit and every exec failure for the full MaxAttempts=5 ladder (codex.go:70-95). A deterministic failure - codex not on PATH, an unknown model id, an expired OAuth session - therefore burns five attempts plus 1+2+4+8s of backoff before surfacing. The comment at codex.go:63-68 claims parity with the HTTP arm on ceiling, deadline and backoff; the missing fourth element, fatal short-circuiting, is not noted.

findings.note: parseCodexEvents assigns the token totals on each turn.completed rather than accumulating them (codex.go:150-158). If one codex exec emits more than one turn.completed, only the last turn's usage is reported and earlier turns' tokens are lost - note the contrast with the caller, which correctly uses v.Tokens.Add across attempts (codex.go:82). Accumulating, or documenting that exec is single-turn by construction, would remove the ambiguity.

evidence.note: tokens = run.TokenTotals{...} replaces any prior turn's totals
v.Tokens = v.Tokens.Add(tokens) accumulates across attempts

findings.note: itoa (codex.go:163-184) reimplements strconv.Itoa to avoid one stdlib import, in a package that already imports fmt for the same purpose (judge.go uses fmt.Sprintf for status formatting). Beyond the duplication, the negation at codex.go:168 overflows for math.MinInt and would return a bare "-"; exit codes make that unreachable today, but the hand-rolled path buys nothing over strconv.Itoa.
